title: Etale cohomology in dimension zero
statement:
Let $k$ be algebraically closed and let $C$ be a separated finite-type
$k$-scheme of dimension at most zero, as allowed in
[def-weil-pbc-eight-curve-assertions]. For an abelian etale sheaf
$F$, its etale cohomology is canonically

$$
 H^q(C,F)=
 \begin{cases}
  \displaystyle\prod_{c\in|C|}F_{\bar c},&q=0,\\
  0,&q>0,
 \end{cases}
$$

where the product is finite and $F_{\bar c}$ denotes the geometric stalk at
$c$.

proof.text:
By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-dim-zero-artinian], the finite-type
zero-dimensional scheme $C$ has finite discrete underlying space and every
point is closed. Let $i:C_{\mathrm{red}}\to C$ be the reduction. By
[lem-weil-pbc-reduction-universal-homeomorphism], $C_{\mathrm{red}}$ is reduced
and $i$ is a universal homeomorphism. Since $C_{\mathrm{red}}$ is a closed
subscheme of the finite-type $k$-scheme $C$, it is itself finite type over $k$.
Applying [lem-weil-pbc-closed-point-residue-field-base] to $C_{\mathrm{red}}$
identifies every residue field $\kappa_{C_{\mathrm{red}}}(c)$ with $k$ (equivalently,
$\mathcal O_{C_{\mathrm{red}},c}=\mathcal O_{C,c}/\sqrt{0}$ has the same
residue field). The singleton pieces of the finite discrete space
$C_{\mathrm{red}}$ are open and closed. Each such piece is affine by
[lem-weil-pbc-finite-discrete-scheme-affine]. Its coordinate ring is reduced
and has only one prime, hence is a field; the residue-field identification
makes that field $k$. Therefore each piece is $\operatorname{Spec}k$. By
[lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family], the morphism from the coproduct of
these pieces to $C_{\mathrm{red}}$ induced by their inclusions is an
isomorphism: its restriction to each summand is the corresponding open
immersion, and the summands are pairwise disjoint and cover $C_{\mathrm{red}}$,
so it is bijective and a local isomorphism.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-geometric-point-coproduct-cohomology] to
the finite coproduct description of $C_{\mathrm{red}}$ from step 1. It gives
vanishing in every degree $q>0$ and identifies degree zero with the finite
product of the geometric stalks on the reduced scheme. The universal
homeomorphism $i$ identifies these cohomology groups with those of $(C,F)$
by [thm-weil-pbc-universal-homeomorphism-invariance]. Under the induced
bijection of points, for the geometric point $\bar c$ over $c$ on
$C_{\mathrm{red}}$ the inverse-image stalk comparison
$(i^{-1}F)_{\bar c}=F_{i\circ\bar c}=F_{\bar c}$ is the canonical one from
[lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-stalk-germ]. Thus the degree-zero product is
$\prod_{c\in|C|}F_{\bar c}$.
